components.duration_note: 24.25 has two branches, a two-week EI wait (a: 2 weeks at 95% funded by the University, then up to ten weeks of EI plus top-up) and no EI wait (b: up to twelve weeks of EI plus top-up). On 2018-03-13 the EI waiting period was one week (EI Act s. 13), so neither branch's condition holds; the University-funded two-week payment is conditional on a two-week EI wait and does not apply (R21, Manitoba example). Coded at branch (b)'s twelve weeks; branch (a) would give ten weeks of top-up. The longer value (15) applies where 24.27 medical leave extends the top-up to the expiry of EI maternity benefits (R13b).

notes: Sources: 2018_00_link (HR tipsheet 'Childbirth & Parental Leave Guidelines - Continuing Academic Staff', updated 9/21/2015); 2018_01 (HR index page: links only, no policy); 2018_02 (Faculty Agreement, July 2017, expiring June 30, 2018).

Governing document: the Faculty Agreement (collective agreement covering staff members appointed to positions in which tenure has been or may be granted, 1.14), in force on 2018-03-13. The tipsheet is a 2015 summary of Article 24; it governs nothing and is used only for details the agreement leaves open.

Birth parent chain: Childbirth Leave up to 15 (c1; top-up c2 within it from week 2, up to 12 weeks at 95%; EI maternity c3 from week 2, 15 weeks) -> Parental Leave up to 10 (c4, also_available; top-up c5 within it) ; EI maternity -> EI parental 35 (c6, consecutive_after c3). Conditional on a physician's certificate: Medical Leave (c7, with full pay c8) from week 12 of the childbirth leave, up to 26 weeks (24.27).
Non-birth parent chain: Parental Leave up to 10 (c4; primary care giver only) with the top-up (c5) within it from week 2, and EI parental 35 (c6) concurrent_with c4 from week 2.

Waiting period: 24.25(a) and 24.35(a) pay two weeks at 95% from the University only 'If EI has determined that there shall be a two-week waiting period'; on 2018-03-13 the EI wait was one week (EI Act s. 13, in force from 2017-01-01), so these payments are not coded (R21, Manitoba example); 24.25(b)/24.35(b) (no waiting period) also do not match a one-week wait. Flagged ambiguous on c2 and c5.

The tipsheet's unpaid extension (total 52 weeks for birth mothers, 37 for male or adoptive primary caregivers) has no counterpart in the agreement other than the Provost's discretionary leave without pay (24.40, c13); coded summary_only (c11), per the rules' source-precedence example for Alberta 2018.

The tipsheet's statement that birth mothers get 'a further 10 weeks of parental leave' omits the agreement's primary-care-giver condition (24.31); the agreement governs (c4 carries caregiver_condition primary).

Not components: Childbirth Leave Replacement Fund (20.12(g), funds replacement staff, not a benefit to the parent); Child-Care Benefit Program (20.12(h), reimbursement of child-care expenses, not leave or pay because of the birth); benefits continuation during childbirth and parental leave (20.14, 24.25(c), 24.35(c)); sabbatical, assisted leave, political leave, special travel, phased retirement (purposes a parent cannot use for a birth).

Documents cited but not saved: Compassionate Care & Emergency Leave terms (Appendix J item 8; flagged on c15); Disability Benefits Program terms and the disability leave regulations (20.12(a), 20.16; flagged on c9); Benefits Guide (20.03.2); the Academic benefits plan (tipsheet); Childbirth & Parental Leave Guidelines - Temporary Academic Staff (linked from 2018_01; covers temporary staff); EFAP New Parent Service (linked from 2018_01); Service Canada EI pages (links); the other Board-AASUA agreements (APO, Librarian, FSO); Universities Academic Pension Plan; GFC Policy Manual 120.9 (Professional Liability) and GFC Policy 44 (Harassment); removal allowance and sabbatical research grant regulations; University Conflict of Interest/Commitment Policy. None of the uncited ones bears on parental leave beyond those flagged.
No calendar term length is stated (Appendix E refers to academic terms without a length); calendar omitted.
